headline_claim: An Artificial Analysis score of 60 is worse than an Arena rating of 1,550 because 1,550 is larger.
sxf_reason: Index points and Bradley–Terry ratings have different scales, populations and meanings.
safer_reading: Treat these as separate evidence signals; never subtract or divide them.

headline_claim: A model preferred by Arena voters must also be top on LiveBench's agentic deliverables.
sxf_reason: Human preference is not identical to objective success on long-horizon tasks.
safer_reading: Compare the same task family or validate your own task outcomes.

headline_claim: A v4.3 index 53 becoming v5 index 59 proves the model improved by six points.
sxf_reason: The evaluation mixture and category weights changed between these index releases.
safer_reading: Compare within a pinned index version; treat cross-version history as a methodology break.

headline_claim: A LiveBench 1.0 aggregate and LiveBench 2.0 overall result can be plotted as one continuous accuracy line.
sxf_reason: LiveBench 2.0 has a different suite design and long-horizon grading surface.
safer_reading: Create separate versioned series and annotate the release transition.

headline_claim: Rank 1 at 1,540 ± 20 is definitely superior to rank 2 at 1,535 ± 23.
sxf_reason: The displayed confidence intervals overlap, so a unique rank is not definitive evidence of superiority.
safer_reading: Read Arena rank spread and compare the confidence bands before declaring a winner.

headline_claim: GPT model at max effort and the same family at low effort are the same benchmark configuration.
sxf_reason: Reasoning effort, model revision and harness settings can materially change cost and score.
safer_reading: Record precise model identifier, effort level, tool setup and provider.

headline_claim: A high Artificial Analysis index guarantees the same model leads multilingual speech translation.
sxf_reason: The AA Intelligence Index is primarily text-based and English-language; speech and multilingual evidence are measured separately.
safer_reading: Find a multilingual speech benchmark or test your exact language workload.

headline_claim: Arena Text preference votes are identical to a factual-correctness guarantee.
sxf_reason: A preferred response can still contain a false claim; Arena separately exposes factuality-oriented analysis.
safer_reading: Use a correctness-specific benchmark and independently fact-check outputs.

headline_claim: The first row on an accuracy-oriented leaderboard is necessarily cheapest and fastest in production.
sxf_reason: Capability, price, latency, throughput and reliability are distinct dimensions.
safer_reading: Combine task-fit evidence with model API price, time to result and failure rate.

headline_claim: Compare two model variants within AA Intelligence Index v5.0.1 with matching published settings.
sxf_reason: Both entries use the same overall scoring method and snapshot, although task relevance still matters.
safer_reading: Use the v5 scores for a shortlist; separately benchmark the actual application.

headline_claim: Compare two models within the same Arena Text filter and snapshot while reporting confidence intervals.
sxf_reason: The pair shares a vote population, metric and snapshot; confidence intervals expose uncertainty.
safer_reading: State the preference category, rating and rank spread rather than claiming absolute correctness.

headline_claim: Compare two models in the same LiveBench 2.0 coding suite using published matching settings.
sxf_reason: A same-suite, same-version result answers a narrower, more meaningful question than comparing overall ranks.
safer_reading: Check details, model setup and cost per successful task; then reproduce on local tasks.
